run_time_bindings.{{SHA256:<module>}}: result_sha256 of the module's settled head bound as CP-5 input (the attempt input's sha256)

run_time_bindings.{{FIG:name}}: as cases/snapshot/submissions.json: the unique T4.10 twelve-month (LTM) Q4 2025 fact of that metric in the CP-1 head; its fact_id is also the fact_id of the verbatim copy in the cp1_references of CP-2 (and CP-3 for the first three); zero or several candidates fail
run_time_bindings.{{TRACE:CP-1 <claim_id>}}: '; '.join('<claim_id>#c<n> <source_id> <locator>') over the bound CP-1 claim's citations, 1-based; each of the seven CP-1 claims must carry at least one citation (asserted), else T5.3 and the 'c1' reference are wrong and the run fails
run_time_bindings.CP-1 claim ids: exactly cash_flow_quality, coverage, data_quality, definition_risks, key_gaps, leverage, liquidity (asserted against the bound CP-1 head: manifest run_time_bindings RT-1; RT-2 zero Python findings; RT-3 at least one citation per CP-1 claim)
run_time_bindings.CP-1 limitation entries: CP-1's own and inherited limitation texts, bound from the CP-1 head at the bind marker of inherited_limitations.sequence
run_time_bindings.T5.5 and T5.8 and T5B.7 rows: T5.5 rows ascending by bound fact_id; T5.8 and T5B.7 inherited rows follow the flattened sequence

binding.signature: view(historical, attempt) -> (sha256, body)  (docs/G1X-OWNER-CORE-PROTOCOL.md section 2; registered in the fixed dict _VIEWS['integrity_review'])
binding.historical: the G1 historical Execution of the ticket's snapshot (owner_workflow._owner_historical): the view is recomputed from the journal, never from the live store, exactly as owners.cp2.view
construction: scope = cp5_integrity.review_scope(historical, attempt); a non-empty scope.issues raises WorkflowError('identity_mismatch')

P(head) = integrity_projection(scope)(head) for the CP-1 head (live.context.integrity_projection: facts a claim names as {ref|unit}, members of an identity group, references a Python check flags) and head.facts, every fact, for every other head

for every modules[*].claims[*]: citations[*] keeps ref, source_id and locator only (the quote key is deleted) and python_findings[i] is cut at its first ': ' (the kind, or 'kind on ref', with no detail)

block['python_findings'][i] = KIND_LABEL[f.kind] + ': ' + f.where for f in python_checks(scope).findings (no detail: the detail of a citation finding can carry a quote fragment); TOOL-CONTRACT ruling 3
binding.digest: sha256 of the UTF-8 body; read_inputs returns it, the journal records it, and the verifier compares it with view(historical, attempt)[0] (owner_workflow._verify_calls_reads; the cp5-tamper-read-body refusal)
binding.no_quote: two conditions (revision 2, F1): (1) no `quote` key at any depth; (2) no citation quote string anywhere in the body except inside CP-3's own T3.3 `*.quote` facts (`shown`, `text`, `label`), which are CP-3's settled market-evidence facts, not citations (P keeps every CP-3 fact and the positive literal names T3.3.m01.quote). No python_findings string carries a detail.

view.body: cp5_integrity.context_block(scope, facts=P) as compact JSON, with every modules[*].claims[*].citations[*].quote removed and python_findings reduced to the kind label plus where (see binding.construction), where P keeps every fact of each head except CP-1, and for CP-1 the facts live.context.integrity_projection keeps

size_probe.what: a measurement on a scratch copy of the S1 positive store (slice-snapshot-positive: CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 restricted; no CP-3 head exists in S1), the same construction as binding.construction, ReviewScope built directly from the stored heads; probe scratchpad/cp5r1/probe/view_size.py, 3.3 s, original store untouched
size_probe.cp3_not_measured: the CP-3 head adds 39 facts and 2 claims in the positive case (28 facts and 1 claim in the gap case) by the CP-3 oracle count; at the CP-2 density (about 290 bytes per fact) that is about 11 KB, an estimate, not a measurement
size_probe.citation_check: of the 24,884 citations of the three heads (mostly CP-1 facts, which the projection omits), none of the quote strings occurs verbatim in the body, and the string "quote" does not occur as a key (S1 has no CP-3 head; on a CP-3 positive head the T3.3.m01.quote and T3.3.m02.quote facts equal the citation quotes of T3.1.i01 and T3.4.preference, the exempt case of view.binding.no_quote)
